text:
maria: heads up — saw a customer report where a temporary operator override flipped routing from 'latency' to 'cost' for a subset of tenants. not expected, seems precedence is weird.

devon: oh no, repro steps?

maria: tenant A had a scoped flag set in console: `route_policy: latency`. ops ran `override route_policy -> cost` for tenant A in emergency. afterwards some requests still went to latency pool and some to cost pool.

lucas: can you paste the override payload? also which runtime version?

maria: payload: ```json
{
  "target": "tenant:A",
  "overrides": {"route_policy": "cost"},
  "ttl": 600
}
```
runtime was `2025.11.3`

beth: we've had discussions about scoped overrides vs inherited defaults — but behavior should be deterministic. sounds like partial application across router shards.

aseem: quick guess: override is written to console and an async fanout pushes to router shards. a race with snapshot rehydration could cause half the shards to apply old snapshot then override, other way around -> inconsistent state. need idempotent apply.

maria: yep that matches logs I pulled. logs show shard-3 applied override at t+2s, shard-7 applied override at t+9s, but router snapshot refresh at t+4s re-applied older config to shard-7.

devon: two parts to fix: 1) make override writes bump config revision so snapshot rehydration rejects older revision. 2) console UX: show 'pending propagation' with per-shard progress so operators can see partial rolls.

lucas: agree. for (1) we can piggyback a monotonic revision field `config_rev` on overrides and snapshots. snapshot apply should check `if incoming_rev < local_rev then ignore`. tiny change in router apply path.

beth: UX wise we should expose a propagation API endpoint `/overrides/:id/status` that returns shards reporting and errors. console can poll until all shards report success or timeout.

maria: also need a rollback/auto-fuse. if more than X% of shards fail to apply in T seconds, auto-revert and notify oncall. 

aseem: for rollout semantics, propose default behavior: overrides are 'atomic at revision' — servers accept only strictly increasing revs. we add a safety window: if rev gap > N, reject and ask for operator confirmation (this avoids accidental big jumps).

devon: implementation plan: router PR to add rev-check + idempotent apply (2 days), console API + small UI indicator + polling (1 day), operator docs + runbook (1 day). Beth can you own console pieces?

beth: I can. I'll mock UI and wire `/overrides/:id/status`. will add a small amber 'partial' state and tooltip explaining shard counts.

lucas: I'll do router changes and add unit tests for race scenarios. also add an integration test that simulates snapshot rehydrates mid-apply.

maria: I'll update runbook and create a short incident drill for oncall to practice safe override rollback.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: router/patch-config-rev-check -> staging at 1765561800.

devon: once staging validates, roll to prod with a quick canary (5% shards) and monitor propagation metric `override.propagation.percent` and `override.apply.errors`. if deviation > 2% abort.

beth: question: should scoped overrides increment tenant-local rev or global config_rev? scoped makes sense — but snapshot rehydration might be global. thoughts?

aseem: each config namespace should have its own rev vector: `{global: N, tenant:<id>: M}`. route resolution uses namespace precedence then compares respective revs. avoid global-only to prevent tenant churn blocking others.

devon: complexity tradeoff. starting with single `config_rev` per scope (global / tenant / service) is fine. don't over-engineer vector clocks yet. document decision.

maria: ack. can we also emit an event `override.propagation.completed` with latency and shard count so billing/telemetry team can correlate?

lucas: yes will add event + tags (override_id, tenant, rev, success_count, total_shards, duration_ms).

beth: I'll add UI to surface the event link for quick debug.

maria: ok agreed. next actions: lucas PR for router, beth API+UI, devon ops rollout plan + metrics alert, aseem runbook changes, maria incident drill.

devon: ping me when staging deploy is green, I'll trigger canary. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks all — I'll file the follow-up ticket and link here: https://redwood.local/ops/ISSUE-4821

deploy-bot: staging deploy succeeded at 1765561905.

devon: staging looks clean. lucas, ready for canary?

lucas: yes, initiating 5% shard canary now.

maria: watching metrics. override.propagation.percent -> 100% in ~7s. nice.

beth: UI shows 'propagated (100%)' and link to event. closing loop: +1 on UX change.

maria: closing this thread — will keep tickets updated. thanks everyone for the quick turn. :party_parrot:
